ex06.title: Mt. Gox explained: why an exchange is not a vault
ex06.reel_caption:
Crypto exchange is not a vault: the Mt. Gox lesson. 🏦

In 2014 the biggest Bitcoin exchange stopped withdrawals. About 850,000 BTC were missing and customers waited a decade for repayments. They didn't hold their own keys.

Holding long-term? Learn self-custody and keep your seed phrase on paper, never online.

trump-swan.title: Trump's company moved $343M of Bitcoin. That's not the real black swan
trump-swan.reel_caption:
Trump Media just moved 4,259 BTC (~$343M) to an exchange. Bitcoin dumped to about $76K the same day, and $1B+ in leveraged trades got wiped out. 🦢

Moved ≠ sold. The twist: those coins were tagged as collateral for a $1B debt that holders can call from 30 Nov.

✅ No borrowed money
✅ Check: transfer or sale?
✅ Emergency fund outside crypto
✅ Only hold what can drop 50%
✅ Don't keep savings on one exchange

trump-swan.li_text:
Trump's company just moved $343 million of Bitcoin to an exchange.

The same day, Bitcoin fell to about $76,000 and more than $1 billion of leveraged trades were force-closed.

But that's not the black swan I'm worried about.

What's confirmed:
→ 4,259 BTC moved to Crypto.com on 5 Nov (on-chain data)
→ The wallets were tagged as collateral for a $1B convertible debt that holders can call from 30 Nov

What's NOT confirmed: a sale. Moving coins to an exchange is usually step one before selling. It isn't proof.

My view: when stocks and crypto fall together, the danger isn't the drop. It's being forced to sell at the bottom.

My 5-point checklist before the next swan:
1. No borrowed money
2. Don't sell on a headline. Check: transfer or sale?
3. Emergency fund outside crypto
4. Only hold what you could watch drop 50%
5. Don't keep your savings on one exchange

Not financial advice. Figures as of 6 Nov 2026.
